summary: China has unilaterally opened visa-free entry of up to 30 days to citizens of dozens of countries — including most of the EU, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and South Korea — while US and Indian citizens still need an embassy visa; a separate 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit scheme covers 50+ nationalities passing through to a third country.

primarySources.name: Department of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China
Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical coverage is strongly recommended — foreign visitors pay for hospital treatment in full, usually up front.

onwardTicket.text: Visa-free entrants and 240-hour transit passengers must be able to show an onward or return ticket; transit passengers need a confirmed ticket to a third country or region.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published, but immigration officers may ask about the purpose of your visit, accommodation and means of support.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency over 5,000 USD (or equivalent) and local currency over 20,000 CNY must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: General Administration of Customs of China — Customs Clearance Guide for International Passengers

notes: Fingerprints are collected from most foreign nationals aged 14–70 on arrival.
Duty-free allowance for visitors: 400 cigarettes and 1.5 liters of alcohol (over 12% vol).
Printed or digital material deemed harmful to China's political interests can be confiscated; drones and satellite communication equipment may require registration.

payments.text: Mobile payment via Alipay and WeChat Pay dominates — both now let foreign visitors link international Visa/Mastercard cards, which is the single most useful thing to set up before arrival. Foreign cards are rarely accepted directly at the point of sale, and cash acceptance is patchy outside banks and larger shops.

safety.text: Violent crime against foreigners is rare and cities are generally very safe. Be aware of local laws: authorities enforce them strictly, and Western governments note risks around arbitrary enforcement and exit bans in specific cases.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — China travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: April–May and September–October offer the most comfortable weather across most of the country; summer is hot and rainy, and northern winters are harsh.

tips.text: Install Alipay or WeChat Pay and link your international card before you fly — most shops, taxis and even street vendors expect QR-code payment, and foreign cards rarely work at the register.
All foreigners must be registered with the police within 24 hours of arrival. Hotels do this automatically; if you stay in a private home, you must register at the local police station yourself.
Many international apps and websites (Google services, WhatsApp, Instagram and others) are blocked in mainland China. Download essential apps, offline maps and translation packs before arrival.

Even if your passport needs a visa for China, the 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit lets eligible nationalities — including US, UK and Canadian citizens — visit without a visa when arriving at an eligible port and continuing to a different country or region.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for China?
faq.answer: Yes, for a regular visit US citizens need a tourist (L) visa, which costs 140 USD and is normally issued valid for 10 years with multiple entries. However, US passport holders transiting to a third country can use the 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit policy at eligible ports instead.

faq.question: Which nationalities can visit China visa-free?
faq.answer: China has unilaterally granted visa-free entry of up to 30 days to citizens of dozens of countries, including most EU members (Germany, France, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland and others), Switzerland, Ireland, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Brazil and Russia. The policy has been extended and expanded several times. Verify your passport's status on cs.mfa.gov.cn before booking.

faq.question: How does China's 240-hour visa-free transit work?
faq.answer: Citizens of 50+ countries — including the US, UK, Canada and Mexico — can enter without a visa for up to 240 hours (10 days) when they arrive at one of the eligible ports and hold a confirmed onward ticket to a third country or region (not back to where they came from). Travel is limited to the permitted regions and you must stay within the 240-hour window.

faq.question: Can I pay with my foreign card in China?
faq.answer: Rarely at the register — China runs on Alipay and WeChat Pay QR payments. Both apps accept international Visa and Mastercard cards for foreign visitors, so set one up before traveling. Keep some cash as a backup; larger banks' ATMs accept foreign cards.

faq.question: Do I have to register with the police in China?
faq.answer: Yes. Every foreigner must have their accommodation registered with the local police within 24 hours of arrival. Hotels handle it during check-in; guests staying in private homes or short-term rentals must go to the nearest police station with their host to register.
